items.text: Melania Trump marks her first year back as first lady with a documentary she produced herself. The film, called Melania, follows the twenty days before Donald Trump returned to the White House for his second term. The movie opened in more than one thousand five hundred theaters in the US and other countries; however, public response remains weak, and interest stays low. Reports show small audiences even in Slovenia, her home country. Many people criticize the timing of the film because protests take place in the US after deadly events involving federal agents . Some viewers feel angry that the president promotes a movie about his wife during a tense period for the country. The film cost about seventy-five million dollars, which makes it one of the most expensive documentaries ever. Big companies help pay for it, and critics say they hope to gain favor with the president. Some countries, including South Africa, refuse to show the film due to poor relations with the US. Difficult words: audience (people who watch a film or show), federal agent (a government worker who enforces national law), favor (support). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Melania Trump made a movie to mark her first year back as first lady. The film follows the days before Donald Trump returns to the White House. It opens in many theaters in the United States and other countries, but not many people go to watch it. Some countries decide not to show the movie at all. Many people are angry about the timing of the film. Protests happen in the United States, and people feel angry that the president cares about a movie during this time. Even in Slovenia, Melania Trump’s home country, only a small number of people watch it. The movie cost seventy-five million dollars. Large companies helped pay for it, and critics say they want to be friends with the president. South Africa doesn’t show the film because of political problems with the United States. Difficult words: mark (to show or celebrate an important time), timing (when something happens), critic (a person who gives opinions, often negative). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Melania Trump makes a movie in her first year back as first lady . The movie shows the days before Donald Trump comes back to the White House. The movie plays in many places, but not many people go to watch it. Some countries do not show it at all. Many people feel angry about the time of the movie. Angry people are in the streets in the United States. People are not happy that the president is talking about the movie now. Melania Trump comes from Slovenia. But in Slovenia, only a few people watch it. The movie needs a lot of money. Big companies help pay for it. South Africa does not show the movie because it has problems with the United States. Difficult words: first lady (the wife of the US president), angry (unhappy about a situation or person), few (a small number). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Canadian actress Catherine O’Hara has died at the age of 71. She was famous for popular films like Home Alone and Beetlejuice , as well as the TV series Schitt’s Creek . She remained active in her career until the end, and many people regarded her as a strong and lively performer. Her death surprised fans and people in the film world. During her long career, O’Hara won many important awards. She received Emmy awards, a Golden Globe, and Screen Actors Guild awards. People praised her for her humor, strong character, and unique style. She became especially well known to a new generation of viewers through her role in Schitt’s Creek . Her agency said she died at her home in Los Angeles after a short illness. Many fans in Canada, the United States, and around the world shared sadness. O’Hara leaves behind a body of work that many people still enjoy and remember. Difficult words: praise (to say good things about someone or their work), unique (special and not like others), body (a lot of something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Canadian actress Catherine O’Hara died at age 71. People know her for movies like Home Alone and Beetlejuice , and the TV show Schitt’s Creek . She worked in film and television for many years, and people loved her humor and style. Her death surprised many fans. O’Hara won several big awards during her career. She won Emmy awards and a Golden Globe. She became very popular again after her role in Schitt’s Creek . Many viewers liked her funny and strong character in the show. Her agency said she died at her home in Los Angeles after a short illness. Fans in Canada and other countries shared sadness . People remember her for her talent and long career. Difficult words: humor (when you know how to make people laugh), award (a prize for good work), sadness (the feeling when something bad happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Catherine O’Hara is a famous actress from Canada. She dies at age 71. Many people know her from the movie Home Alone and the show Schitt’s Creek . She is funny, and many people love her work. She wins many awards in her life. She wins Emmy awards and a Golden Globe. People like her roles in movies and TV shows. She works for many years. Her family says she dies at her home in Los Angeles after a short illness . Fans feel sad. People remember her films and shows. Difficult words: age (how old someone is), award (what you get for good work), illness (the time when somebody is sick). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Atomic scientists move the Doomsday Clock closer to midnight than ever before. The clock now stands at eighty-five seconds to midnight, which shows extreme danger for the world. Experts say this danger comes from nuclear weapons, weak global control, wars, climate problems, and the fast growth of AI. Many people see the clock as a clear warning about how close the world is to disaster. Scientists point to aggressive actions by the United States, Russia, and China. They worry about nuclear threats, weak arms agreements, and ongoing wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. They also fear the use of AI in the military and the spread of false information. Climate change adds more pressure to an already unstable situation. Experts say global leaders fail to work together and protect peace. Nuclear agreements fall apart, and trust between countries continues to fall. Scientists warn that without strong cooperation and clear rules, the risk of global disaster will continue to rise. Difficult words: ongoing (happening now and not finished), pressure (a strong push or stress that makes someone act), cooperation (people or countries working together). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Atomic scientists move the Doomsday Clock closer to midnight than ever before. The clock now shows eighty-five seconds to midnight. This means the world faces danger. Scientists warn about nuclear weapons, wars, climate problems, and new technology like AI. The experts worry about actions by the United States, Russia, and China. These countries show more power and less trust . Wars in Ukraine and the Middle East worry people, too. Nuclear deals don’t work, and leaders fail to work together. AI also helps spread false news and creates new risks. Scientists say world leaders must do something fast. They need to talk, trust each other, and protect peace . Without change, danger for the world will grow. Difficult words: doomsday (a time of very great danger or the end of the world), trust (belief that someone is honest and will do the right thing), peace (life without war or fighting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists move the Doomsday Clock very close to midnight. The clock shows eighty-five seconds to midnight. This means that the world is not safe at all. Scientists feel worried about nuclear weapons, war, climate problems, and new technology. The United States, Russia, and China act in strong and risky ways. Experts worry about war in Ukraine and the Middle East. Countries do not work well together. Old rules about nuclear weapons do not help anymore. Scientists ask leaders to do something now. They want peace , clear rules, and honest talk. Without help, danger grows for everyone. Difficult words: doomsday (a time close to the end of the world), act (to do something, not only talk), peace (life without war). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Gold prices reach record levels above 5,000 dollars per ounce. Many people move their money into gold because they feel worried about political and economic problems in the world. Silver and platinum prices also rise at the same time. Precious metals feel safer to many investors than paper money during times of uncertainty. Central banks play a big role in this rise, because they change how they store their money and depend less on the US dollar. Trade tensions also increase fear. The US government talks about very high taxes on goods from other countries. These messages cause worry about future trade and push more investors toward gold. Another reason comes from possible lower interest rates in the United States. When rates fall, gold becomes more attractive than money in banks. In the past, gold prices rise during crises , but this increase feels different. The price grows more than ninety percent in just over one year, which makes this moment unusual in history. Difficult words: precious (very valuable and special), tension (a feeling of worry or stress), crisis (a very bad and difficult situation). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Gold prices are the highest ever. Many people buy gold because they worry about money and world problems. Silver and platinum prices rise as well. People trust gold when they worry about the future. Central banks buy more gold and use the US dollar less than before. Trade problems make people feel nervous. The US president talks about very high taxes on goods from other countries which scare markets and push people to choose gold. People also expect lower interest rates in the United States. Lower rates make gold more interesting than bank savings. In the past, gold prices rose during hard times, but this rise happens much faster. The price grows very quickly in a short time. Difficult words: platinum (a special metal which people use for jewelry), tax (money people pay to the government), market (a place where people buy and sell). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prices of gold go very high now. Many people buy gold because they feel afraid about the world. Prices of silver and platinum go up too. People think that gold is safe money. Big banks in many countries buy more gold. They use the US dollar less. Problems between countries make people worry. These worries push people to choose gold. Banks in the United States lower interest rates . Low rates make gold a good idea for many people. In hard times before, prices of gold go up, too. But now it happens very fast. Difficult words: platinum (a special metal), push (to make something happen or move), interest rate (the extra money which you pay to the bank if you want to borrow money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Salmon is one of the most popular fish eaten in Europe; however, wild salmon populations stay low after many years of overfishing . Most salmon that people eat today doesn’t come from rivers. It comes from fish farms in other countries, especially Norway. Farming salmon helps protect wild fish, but it also creates new problems for nature and for the fish themselves. Many salmon farms use open cages in the sea, which means waste, chemicals, and food leftovers go straight into the water and cause pollution. Animal welfare groups also worry about crowded cages where sea lice spread fast and can harm or kill young fish. Farmers often use strong chemicals to fix this problem. Critics say people don’t see these issues because everything happens underwater. Some farms try to work in a better way and follow higher standards . Labels like ASC help buyers find fish that should meet certain rules. However, experts warn that a label doesn’t always mean a farm causes no harm. Difficult words: overfishing (catching too many fish so there are not enough left in the sea), leftover (food or things that are not eaten or used), standard (a rule about how something should be done). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Salmon is a very common fish in Europe, but there are fewer wild salmon today. Because of this, most salmon comes from fish farms in other countries. Norway sells the largest amount to the EU. Fish farming helps stop catching too many fish, but it also creates new problems. Many farms keep salmon in open sea cages. Waste and chemicals go into the water and harm the environment. Fish often live very close together, so diseases spread fast. It hurts the fish, and farmers must use chemicals to solve the problems. Animal groups say this causes pain and stress for salmon. Some farms follow better rules and use special labels . These labels help people choose better fish, but experts say they do not always stop problems at every farm. Difficult words: common (usual, normal), amount (how much of something there is), label (a sign or mark on a product that gives information). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people in Europe eat salmon . There are not many wild salmon now. People eat farm salmon. Most farm salmon comes from other countries, usually from Norway. Fish farms help save wild fish. But they have problems too. Many farms keep fish in sea cages . Dirty water and chemicals go into the sea. Fish live very close to each other. When a fish gets sick, other fish get sick too. Farmers use strong chemicals to stop this. People do not see these problems underwater. Some farms try to care for fish better. Labels help people choose better salmon. But labels do not always mean that the fish live well. Difficult words: salmon (a large fish with pink meat), wild (not from a farm), cage (a space where people keep animals inside). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

CEO pay in the United States has grown very fast since the late 20th century. The gap between very rich leaders and normal workers has become much wider. Tesla CEO Elon Musk may become the first trillionaire CEO after approval of a very large pay deal. Other big company leaders also earn far more than before, and high pay now appears common in large companies. Many investors believe that strong leaders directly affect company success, so they accept very high rewards. CEO pay doesn’t come as one salary. It usually includes salary, bonuses , and mostly company stock linked to the company’s value. Musk gets no salary, only stock, and he earns more shares when Tesla meets clear targets. This system aims to push CEOs to focus on long-term growth, not quick gains. Supporters say high pay rewards skill and good results. Critics say pay often rises without clear proof of better work. Studies show weak links between pay and performance, while worker pay stays almost flat. This growing gap brings questions about fairness and the future of pay systems. Difficult words: approval (saying yes to something officially), bonus (extra money you get for good work), stock (a small part of a company you can own). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

CEO pay in the US has grown very fast since the 1990s, and the pay gap between CEOs and workers is much bigger than before. Elon Musk may become the first trillionaire CEO because Tesla approved a very large pay deal. Other big company leaders also earn much more money, and high CEO pay is now normal in large companies. CEO pay doesn’t come from one paycheck . It includes salary, bonuses, and is mostly a part of the company. It means that a CEO’s pay is connected to the company’s success. Musk earns stock only if Tesla is successful. Many companies now use this system to push CEOs to think about a company’s future, not only about their money. Some people say high pay brings strong leaders and better results . Others say CEO pay rises even when results are not good. Studies show worker pay grows slowly, while CEO pay grows fast. This makes people speak about fair pay. Difficult words: pay gap (the difference in how much money different people earn), paycheck (the money you get for your work, usually each month or week), result (what happens because of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

CEO pay in the US grows very fast. The money gap between CEOs and workers is very big. Elon Musk gets a very large pay deal from Tesla. Other big company bosses also get much more money. High CEO pay is now normal in big companies. CEO pay is not one money. There is extra money and company stock. Company stock is a part of a company. When the company makes a lot of money, the CEO gets more money. Elon Musk gets stock when Tesla does well. This way is better for companies. CEOs want the company do well. Many people say that high pay helps companies grow. Other people say that it is not fair. Worker pay grows very slowly. CEO pay grows very fast. Many people ask if this system is good or not. Difficult words: pay (money for work), money gap (the different money which different people get), extra (more than usual). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nilofer Merchant suggests a simple idea that can improve both health and productivity : turning one-on-one meetings into walking meetings. Instead of sitting in offices or cafés, people can walk while discussing their work. This method helps reduce the risks linked to long periods of sitting, which include heart disease, diabetes, and even certain types of cancer. Merchant shares her personal experience of being invited to a walking meeting. At first, it felt unusual, but she soon realized its benefits. Now, she walks up to 30 miles a week while having meetings. Walking meetings allow people to stay active without sacrificing work time. They also encourage creative thinking by taking people out of their usual office environment. She believes that many problems seem like opposites, but they don’t have to be. Health and work can go together, just like walking and meetings. Fresh air and movement can bring fresh ideas, making work both effective and enjoyable. Difficult words: productivity (the ability to get work done efficiently), sacrifice (to give up something important). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Nilofer Merchant has a simple idea of staying healthy and working better: walking meetings. Instead of sitting in offices or cafés, people can walk while they talk. Sitting too much is bad for health and can cause heart disease, diabetes , and even cancer. Walking meetings help people move more without losing work time. Merchant started doing walking meetings after someone invited her to one. At first, she thought it was strange , but later, she saw how useful it was. Now, she walks many miles each week while having meetings. Walking helps her think better and feel healthier. She believes that we don’t have to choose between work and health. We can do both at the same time. Walking and talking bring new ideas, making work more interesting and creative . Difficult words: diabetes (a disease in which the body cannot control the level of sugar in the blood), strange (unusual), creative (having new ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nilofer Merchant says that we can work and be healthy at the same time. She has a simple idea: walking meetings. Instead of sitting, we can walk when we talk. Sitting too much is bad for health and can make people sick. Walking helps us feel better. Merchant first tries a walking meeting when someone invites her. At first, it is strange. But she likes the idea. Now, she walks a lot every week while working. Walking meetings help her think better and stay active . She says that we do not have to stop working to be healthy. We can do both together. Walking and talking help people get new ideas and feel good. Difficult words: instead of (in place of someone or something else), invite (to ask someone to come somewhere), active (busy, doing something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European Union leaders held an emergency meeting after rising tension with the United States over Greenland and possible trade punishment . The concern followed comments by President Donald Trump about taking control of Greenland and using tariffs against European allies . EU leaders said they would defend themselves against pressure and said that only Denmark and Greenland can decide Greenland’s future. After the meeting, Trump pulled back his threats of tariffs and said a deal with the NATO leader could help the United States reach its goals. EU officials welcomed this change and said the situation looked calmer than a day earlier. They showed support for Denmark and Greenland, and also for EU countries that faced trade threats. However, there are still many questions. The details of the deal with NATO are unclear, and Trump repeated that Greenland matters for US and global security. European leaders said they accept more US defense but disagreed with any change of borders. Denmark’s prime minister later traveled to Greenland for talks. Difficult words: punishment (something bad you do to someone because they break a rule), ally (a country or person that helps and supports you), threat (a sign or warning that someone may do something bad). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

EU leaders met in an emergency meeting because of problems with the United States over Greenland. President Trump spoke about taking control of Greenland and using tariffs against EU countries. The EU said it will protect itself and said only Denmark and Greenland can decide what happens to Greenland. Later, Trump pulled back his words about tariffs and said a deal with NATO could solve the problem. EU leaders felt much happier than the day before. They said it was important to stick together and show support for Denmark and Greenland. Still, the problem is not over. Trump said Greenland is important to keep the US and the world safe. EU leaders said they accept more US soldiers but don’t agree with any change of borders. Denmark’s prime minister traveled to Greenland after the meeting. Difficult words: tariff (a tax on things from another country), pull back (to stop or take back a plan or action), stick together (to stay united and support each other). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

EU leaders meet because of problems with the United States. President Trump talks about Greenland and special taxes for some European countries. The EU says that it will protect itself. The EU says that only Denmark and Greenland can decide about Greenland. Trump later stops his words about taxes. He says that a deal with NATO can help. EU leaders feel calm. They say that working together helps. They want to help Denmark and Greenland. But the problem does not end yet. Trump says that Greenland is important to keep the US and the world safe. The EU says yes to more US soldiers but no to new borders . Denmark’s leader goes to Greenland to talk. Difficult words: tax (money which people or companies pay to the government), protect (to keep safe), border (a line between countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iran is not one of the world’s largest oil producers; however, recent protests in the country have pushed oil prices higher. Investors worry that conflict could reduce oil supply at a time when the global market has little extra oil available. Even fear alone can move prices, because traders react quickly to risk. That’s why oil markets responded strongly to events in Iran. Iran produces much less oil than countries like the United States or Saudi Arabia, and sanctions limit where it can sell its oil. Most Iranian oil now goes to China. Still, Iran sits near the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow sea route where about one-fifth of the world’s oil passes. Any trouble there could slow oil transport and affect many countries. Only a few oil producers have spare capacity, and Saudi Arabia holds most of it. If Iranian oil exports stopped, others couldn’t easily replace them. Oil supply is stable for now, but the political situation in the area worries many people. Difficult words: sanction (an official limit by governments), route (a path or way to go from one place to another, like a road or sea path), spare (a path for travel). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Iran is not one of the world’s largest oil producers; however, recent protests in the country have pushed oil prices higher. Investors worry that conflict could reduce oil supply at a time when the global market has little extra oil available. Even fear alone can move prices, because traders react quickly to risk. That’s why oil markets responded strongly to events in Iran. Iran produces much less oil than countries like the United States or Saudi Arabia, and sanctions limit where it can sell its oil. Most Iranian oil now goes to China. Still, Iran sits near the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow sea route where about one-fifth of the world’s oil passes. Any trouble there could slow oil transport and affect many countries. Only a few oil producers have spare capacity, and Saudi Arabia holds most of it. If Iranian oil exports stopped, others couldn’t easily replace them. Oil supply is stable for now, but the political situation in the area worries many people. Difficult words: sanction (an official limit by governments), route (a path or way to go from one place to another, like a road or sea path), spare (a path for travel). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Iran makes some oil, but not as much as big oil countries. Protests in Iran make oil prices go up. People are worried. Only this can also make oil prices go up. Iran cannot sell oil freely , so it sells mainly to China. Iran is near a narrow sea route . Many oil ships pass there. If problems grow bigger, ships cannot get through. Only one country has much extra oil ready. If Iran stops selling oil, others cannot help quickly. Higher oil prices mean higher prices for people. Travel and transport cost more. Difficult words: protest (an action where people show that they are unhappy about something), freely (easily, openly), route (a way to go from one place to another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Amid a legal battle over the ingredients of Cyprus’s famous Halloumi cheese, former airline pilot Pantelis Panteli has emerged as a champion of tradition. After losing his job, Panteli turned to cheese-making, exclusively using ewe’ s milk despite industry trends favoring cow’s milk. His ‘Kouella’ brand has gained popularity despite limitations on production. The debate over Halloumi’s ingredients has sparked protests among farmers and concerns about production capacity. Authorities aim to delay full compliance with new regulations until 2029. While some argue for a blend of milk to cater to international tastes, others, like Panteli, advocate for preserving the traditional recipe, emphasizing the unique flavor of ewe’ milk. Difficult words: ewe (a female sheep), compliance (conforming to rules or regulations), cater (provide food and drink). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Former pilot Pantelis Panteli now makes traditional Cyprus’s Halloumi cheese with ewe’ s milk. He fights against industry which now prefers using cow’s milk. Panteli’s production of the ‘Kouella’ brand is not too big but it became very popular. The debate over Halloumi’s ingredients led to protests among farmers and worries about production. Officials plan to delay full compliance with regulations until 2029. Some farmers argue that it is necessary to choose the right milk to suit international tastes, but others, like Panteli, prefer to keep traditions alive. Difficult words: ewe (a female sheep), debate (a fight or argument), compliance (when you have to follow rules). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A former pilot Pantelis Panteli loses his job. He now makes traditional cheese in Cyprus. The cheese is called Halloumi. It is popular worldwide. Panteli uses ewe’s milk. Ewe is a female sheep. Its milk tastes different. Panteli does not make a lot of cheese, but people love it. Most farmers use cow’s milk. They say that people in the world prefer cow’s milk. Farmers worry about new rules. They delay them. The new rules will be in 2029. Some farmers want to change the cheese. But Panteli says no. He wants to keep Cyprus’s tradition alive . Difficult words: traditional (something what exists for a long time), delay (to make late or slow), alive (not dead). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Taiwan has one of the best recycling systems in the world. In the past, the country had serious trash problems; however, strong rules changed people’s daily habits . People pay for waste that they cannot recycle, so they try to produce less trash. Cities remove most public bins, which means people keep their waste until special trucks arrive several times a week. This system makes people more responsible and reduces cheating. The government works with private companies that collect and sort waste. A national recycling fund supports these companies, and producers and importers pay into it. This rule makes companies responsible for the plastic they sell. AI robots help sort many kinds of materials faster than humans, but workers still handle difficult tasks. Taiwan recycles most household plastic, and only a small amount goes to burning plants. Still, some weak plastic cannot return to use and ends in fire plants. The system shows strong results, but it also has limits. Difficult words: habit (something you do often and usually without thinking), fund (money saved for a purpose), importer (a person or company that brings goods into a country from another country). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Taiwan has a strong recycling system that helps reduce trash . People pay for waste which they cannot recycle, so they try to use less plastic. Cities put away public trash bins , and special trucks collect waste often. This rule makes people keep their own trash and follow the system. Private companies collect and sort the waste, and the government supports them with money. Producers and importers pay money because they are also responsible for plastic waste. AI robots sort plastic, metal, and paper, but workers still help with difficult tasks. Taiwan recycles most plastics, but low quality plastic goes to fire plants. Taiwan shows how rules and technology can work together. Difficult words: trash (things you do not want and throw away), trash bin (a container where people put trash), importer (a person or company that brings goods into a country from another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Taiwan has a good recycling system. People pay money for trash which they cannot recycle. Therefore, they try to make less trash. Cities have no trash bins on the streets. Big trucks come many times each week. People keep their trash at home until the truck comes. Companies collect trash, and the government helps them with money. Shops and factories also pay money to help recycle plastic. AI robots sort trash into plastic, metal, and paper. Most trash can return to use, but some plastic goes to fire plants. Taiwan shows that good rules help people care about trash. Difficult words: recycle (to use old things and materials again and not throw them away), trash (things which you do not want and throw away), trash bin (a container where people put trash). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Swiss inventor has presented a new version of the Sarco pod, a machine that helps people end their lives in places where the law allows assisted death . The new model would allow two people to enter together and would use AI to decide if a person is mentally able to choose death. The creator says software could judge people more fairly than doctors. The idea has caused a strong debate. Many experts say AI cannot safely decide such serious questions and can make mistakes. They warn that a machine shouldn’t replace human medical judgment in life and death decisions. Some also question whether the device causes a peaceful death, as claimed. Assisted suicide remains legal in Switzerland under loose rules, but it stays illegal or tightly controlled in many countries. Past use of the Sarco pod led to police action and legal concern. As laws differ around the world, the new proposal raises fresh ethical and legal questions. Difficult words: assisted death (when a person gets help to die, usually because they are very sick), differ (to not be the same), ethical (about what is right or wrong). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A Swiss man showed a new suicide machine which can take two people at the same time. The pod would use AI to test if a person has a clear mind before they choose to die. He says a computer can decide better than a doctor. Many doctors and ethics experts don’t agree. They say AI often makes mistakes and can’t understand human feelings well enough. They worry that machines will make final choices for people. Switzerland allows assisted suicide under certain rules, but many countries don’t. One past case with the pod caused police action and a strong public debate. The new plan brings more questions about law, safety, and ethics. Difficult words: suicide (when a person ends their own life), ethics (ideas and rules about right and wrong acting), choice (choosing between more things), assisted suicide (when a person gets help to die, usually because they are very sick). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A man in Switzerland shows a new machine for assisted death . The machine lets two people get in together. It uses an AI to check the mind of a person. The person then chooses to die. Many people do not like this idea. Doctors say that AI cannot understand people well. They worry that AI can be wrong. In Switzerland, it is possible to choose assisted death. The country has rules for it. But in many other countries, it is not possible. The new machine makes people worry. They do not believe the rules. They do not think that it is a safe way to die. Difficult words: assisted death (when a person gets help to die, usually because they are very sick), mind (your thinking and feelings), rule (an official instruction which tells you what you can or cannot do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ivory Coast plans to buy the entire volume of cocoa that farmer groups cannot sell. The government wants to make sure farmers still receive money even though cocoa prices fall to the lowest level in two years. Cocoa plays a very important role in the country because it makes up a large part of the economy and supports many families. Exports slow down after chocolate makers use less cocoa when prices rise before. This situation causes large cocoa stocks to build up. The government now steps in and works with trusted local companies and international buyers to collect and buy the cocoa. Officials say this plan should protect farmers and keep the market stable. Ivory Coast produces more cocoa than any other country in the world. About one out of five people depends on this work for their income. With prices down by about five dollars per kilo, many farmers face problems. The government hopes this action will support producers and prevent serious economic damage. Difficult words: entire (whole, not missing any part), stock (goods that people keep to sell later), prevent (to stop something from happening). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Ivory Coast says it will buy all unsold cocoa from farmer groups. The government wants farmers to get their money while cocoa prices fall to the lowest point in two years. Prices drop by about five dollars per kilo. Exports slow after chocolate companies use less cocoa. Therefore, a lot of cocoa stay in storage . The government works with local buyers and big international companies to buy and move the cocoa. Leaders say this plan will help farmers and calm the market. Ivory Coast grows more cocoa than any other country. Cocoa is important for many people and brings money to the country. Many people depend on this work to live. The government hopes this move will protect jobs and incomes. In the Paris suburb of Romainville, an urban farm brings the community together. The place offers jobs, learning activities, and fresh food at fair prices. Families, older people, and children all use the space, and many local people say it improves life in the area. The farm also runs events where people can meet and feel part of the community. Once a week, the farm holds a small market. Prices depend on a person’s income , so people with less money pay much less. Many people in the area live with very little money, so this system helps them buy healthy food. Staff check income levels in a simple way and give large discounts when needed. For older residents with small pensions , the market is very important because it helps them eat well and feel included . Local leaders say this project builds trust and care between people and could inspire other cities to do the same. Difficult words: income (money a person receives), pension (money a person gets regularly after they stop working), include (to make someone part of a group or activity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Rumen Radev, the president of Bulgaria, says he will resign and start a new political party. He made this move only two months before the early elections. Bulgaria has a political system in which the government depends on parliament, rather than the president. According to Radev, democracy is in danger because of corruption , secret deals, and extreme views. He plans to run for prime minister, a move that many people have been expecting for a long time. Radev says people feel unhappy even after Bulgaria joins the Schengen area and the eurozone. Many people stop voting because they don’t trust politicians, courts, or the media. Radev says protests show deep anger in society. During his time as president, he has named seven temporary governments because parties couldn’t work together. Radev also speaks about foreign policy and the war near Bulgaria. Some people call him pro-Russian; however, he says he wants peace and safety. He also supports a public vote on the euro, which the parliament refuses. The vice president will take his role after Radev resigns. Difficult words: resign (to leave a job by your own choice), corruption (dishonest or illegal use of power for money or advantage), temporary government (a short-term government that runs the country until a new one forms). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Bulgarian President Rumen Radev says he will leave his job and start a new political party. He wants to run for prime minister before early elections . He says corrupt leaders and secret businesses hurt democracy . Bulgaria had many elections and several governments because parties couldn’t form a good government. Radev says many people feel poor and unsafe even after Bulgaria joins the eurozone. Many people stop voting because they don’t trust courts, politicians, or the media. Large protests show strong public anger. He also speaks about the war near Bulgaria and says peace matters most. Some people say that Radev is close to Russia, but he doesn’t agree with that. After he leaves his job, the vice president will become president. Difficult words: elections (public votes to choose leaders), corrupt (dishonest and willing to break rules for personal profit), democracy (a system where people choose their leaders by voting). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There are big protests in the streets. Many people do not have money. Even after Bulgaria starts using the Euro. Radev wants a safe country. He wants people to vote on the euro, but the parliament says no. After he leaves, the vice president takes his place. Difficult words: party (a political group with similar ideas), prime minister (the boss of a government), elections (when people vote to choose leaders). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brooklyn Beckham shared a long post on Instagram where he spoke about deep problems with his parents. He said his parents cared more about public promotion and endorsements than about his feelings. He also said they treated his wife badly and caused stress around their wedding. He wrote that he felt hurt and angry for a long time and decided to speak openly. In his post, Brooklyn said his mother took over the first dance at his wedding, even though he and his wife had planned it earlier. He also said his mother promised to make his wife’s wedding dress, but then stopped at the last moment. Because of this, his wife had to find another dress very quickly. Brooklyn said these events showed a lack of care and respect. The post came as David Beckham spoke at a public event about family and social media networking. The family hasn’t answered Brooklyn’s claims. Brooklyn said he doesn’t plan to reconcile with this family and feels calmer after stepping away from it. Difficult words: endorsement (public support for a product, person, or idea), treat (to behave toward someone in a certain way), reconcile (to become friendly again after a fight). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Brooklyn said he didn’t want to make peace now and felt better after moving away from his family. Difficult words: fame (when many people know you), public image (the way people see a person in public), peace (times without a conflict). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A study in The Lancet predicts that by 2050, more than half of all adults and a third of young people worldwide will be overweight or obese. Researchers warn that obesity rates are expected to rise quickly, especially in lower-income countries. The study forecasts that China, India, and the US will have the largest number of overweight individuals. Additionally, sub-Saharan Africa is expected to experience a significant increase in obesity due to population growth, with numbers rising by over 250%. Experts describe obesity as a global pandemic and highlight the serious health risks it brings. They emphasize that governments must act now to prevent a major crisis. The study also shows that obesity often increases as economies grow and food becomes more accessible. While obesity trends differ across regions, the report provides valuable data to help countries address the issue effectively. Without intervention , the number of people with obesity could more than double by 2050, leading to severe health and economic consequences . Difficult words: differ (to be different or unlike), intervention (actions taken to solve a problem), consequence (the result or effect of an action). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

China, India, and the US will have the most overweight people. Also, sub-Saharan Africa will see a big rise in obesity because of its growing population. Experts call obesity a global problem because it causes many health issues . They say governments must do something now to stop this bad situation. The study also shows that as countries become richer more people get overweight because food is easier to get. If nothing changes, the number of obese people may more than double, which will bring serious health and money problems. Difficult words: obese (very fat), obesity (when someone is very fat), issue (a problem). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

When countries get richer, people eat more food. They become fat. Every country is different , but the report has good information to help. If nothing changes, there will be many more overweight people. Many more people will be sick because of that. Difficult words: overweight (fat), obesity (when someone is very fat), different (not the same or similar). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA has begun moving the Artemis II rocket from its assembly point to the launch area at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. The rocket travels only four miles; however, the trip can take up to twelve hours because it moves very slowly. Less than one mile per hour. Engineers want to keep the rocket safe as it goes over roads and small hills. This crewed mission will be the first time since the Apollo missions of the 1960s and 70s that people travel toward the Moon. Four astronauts will fly inside a space capsule on top of the rocket. They will travel around the Moon and then return to Earth after about ten days. Its main goal is to check that all systems work well with people on board. NASA plans to launch the rocket as early as 6 February if conditions allow it. While it will take astronauts around the Moon rather than touching down, the flight will help prepare future missions that aim to land people on the Moon again. Scientists also see it as an important step before future human travel to Mars. Difficult words: assembly (putting parts together to make something), crewed (having people on board), condition (the state something is in). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA started to move the Artemis II rocket to the launch area in Florida. The rocket travels at four miles per hour and takes up to twelve hours because it moves so slowly. Workers guide it carefully so it stays safe on the road. This mission will send people toward the Moon for the first time since the Apollo missions in the 1960s and 70s. Four astronauts will travel inside a capsule on top of the rocket. They will fly around the Moon and then come back to Earth after ten days. The crew will not land on the Moon; the team wants to check that all systems work well with people inside the spacecraft. NASA plans the launch for early February if the weather and systems stay good. This mission helps NASA prepare for future trips that will put people on the Moon again and later support travel to Mars. Difficult words: launch (to send into space), guide (to show the way or help someone move safely), capsule (a small space vehicle). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite its high cost of 55,000 euros, pet cloning is becoming more popular in Spain. Christian Morales, a 33-year-old from Barcelona, lost his beloved French Bulldog, Lola. He preserved her DNA in a laboratory to keep the possibility of seeing her again. Although he hasn’t decided to clone her yet, he hopes that prices will become more affordable in the future. A lab in southern Spain, which previously focused on cloning expensive horses, now offers cloning services for dogs and cats. Scientists explain that cloned pets are nearly identical to the original in appearance and behavior. However, psychologists argue that cloning cannot bring back a pet’s consciousness or memories, meaning owners still experience grief. Despite ethical concerns, demand for pet cloning remains strong, with many owners seeking to bring back their beloved animals. Christian continues paying 500 euros a year to store Lola’s DNA, imagining a future where he can again have a version of his childhood pet. Difficult words: cloning (creating an exact copy of a living thing), consciousness (awareness and thoughts of a living being). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The cloned pet looks and behaves like the original, but experts say it will not have the same memories or feelings. Psychologists believe cloning doesn’t stop sadness after losing a pet. Even though some people worry about cloning, many owners still want it. Christian pays 500 euros a year to keep Lola’s DNA and hopes he can see her again one day. Difficult words: clone (to make an exact copy of a living thing), DNA (a molecule in your body which has genetic information in it), behave (to act in a certain way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
